title: U.S. housing starts fell 5.2% in September to a 1.22 million pace
summary: Census Bureau data showed September housing starts at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1,221,000, down 5.2% from August and 7.4% from a year earlier; permits were 1,400,000.
body: Privately owned housing starts ran at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1,221,000 in September 2026, 5.2% below the revised August estimate of 1,288,000 and 7.4% below September 2025, the Census Bureau reported on October 20.

Single-family starts were 859,000, down 4.6% from August. Building permits, an early signal of future construction, were 1,400,000, about flat from August and 3.0% below a year earlier. Single-family permits fell 4.0% to 845,000.
Completions rose 2.2% from August to 1,192,000 but were 14.0% lower than a year earlier. The Census Bureau notes that several of these monthly changes are within the survey's margin of error.
why: Fewer new homes being started means less new supply competing with resale houses and rentals in coming years. If you invest in fast-growing suburbs, watch local permit counts alongside these national numbers.
source_name: U.S. Census Bureau: New Residential Construction, September 2026
